To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we present a new model for multi-modal learning of abstract concept embeddings, (2) we show that our model is able to propagate perceptual information from concrete concepts to abstract ones, (3) we show that this model outperforms previous models in the ability to learn abstract concepts, (4) we show that the model is able to learn abstract concepts from a single modality

we present a novel method for combining perceptual and linguistic information to learn semantic embeddings of both concrete and abstract concepts, and that we demonstrate that this method performs better than previous alternatives.

(1) the performance of multi-modally trained language models on abstract concepts can be improved via an embedding approach that combines information from distinct modalities and that propagates perceptual features of concrete concepts to abstract ones, and (2) the proposed approach is superior to previous methods for combining information from distinct modalites and for propagating perceptual information to abstract concepts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning abstract concepts from multi-modal data, and the question of what the most appropriate representation for such concepts is.
how we can learn representations of abstract lexical concepts using multi-modal data.
the problem of acquiring semantic representations from both natural language and visual input, and the implications for theories of abstract concepts and language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the model we propose in this paper is the first of its kind, in that it is a multi-modal model that learns embeddings of abstract concepts, and it is the best performing multi-modal model to date, outperforming all previous models in terms of the quality of the embeddings of both concrete and abstract concepts that it produces.

we present a novel approach that learns multimodel embeddings and that outperforms other approaches in combining information from distinct modalities and propagating perceptual information on more abstract concepts.
our work shows how to combine perceptual and linguistic data to learn representations that are useful for a wide variety of tasks, including the acquisition of abstract conceptual information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model can learn the meaning of abstract concepts by combining the meaning of concrete concepts, which are more easily learned by the model.

the proposed method is capable to learn abstract concept representations from both linguistic (text) and perceptual (image) input and that these representations are more effective than previous approaches.
we are able to learn abstract concepts from multimodal data, and we are able to show that the performance of multimodal models is better than unimodal models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to learn abstract semantic concepts from multi-modal data, and that doing so is advantageous over learning from unimodal language data alone.
, in order to acquire abstract concepts, models need to learn to integrate information across different modalities and to use this information to disambiguate the meanings of abstract words.
abstract concepts can be learned from perceptual input, and that multi-modal models have a significant role to play in this process.
